content.user_title: Assess Data Value and Prioritize Opportunities
content.value_statement: Organizations often overlook valuable uses for their data or cannot explain where value originates. This skill provides structured diagnosis, measurement guidance, and prioritized improvement actions.
actual_capabilities: Classifies opportunities across nine data value types.
Scores five value factors and identifies the weakest factor.
Maps data by source, form, scale, quality, and scenario.
Ranks internal and external scenarios by scale, value, and competition.
Separates realized value from potential value for measurement.
Proposes value improvement actions and timing priorities.
limitations: It does not issue licensed asset valuations or regulatory opinions.
Financial estimates depend on evidence, assumptions, and user-provided inputs.
Cross-industry opportunities require separate legal and authorization review.
The framework does not replace buyer research or market validation.

use_cases.title: Map overlooked value
use_cases.description: Review a data portfolio across nine value types and identify evidence gaps.

use_cases.title: Prioritize product scenarios
use_cases.description: Compare candidate data products and rank their most credible use scenarios.

use_cases.title: Prepare investment decisions
use_cases.description: Separate realized benefits from potential value and identify improvement priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Identify value types
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this dataset across all nine value types. For each type, state relevance, evidence, and missing information.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose value factors
prompt_templates.prompt: Score the five value factors from one to five. Explain each score, identify the weakest factor, and recommend improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Rank value scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these internal and external scenarios by market scale, buyer value, competition, compliance, and evidence. Rank them with stated assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Build an assessment report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete data value assessment. Include value types, five-factor diagnosis, data map, scenario ranking, measurement ranges, decay risks, and actions.

output_examples.input: Assess customer service transcripts for overlooked value.
output: Strongest value: cost reduction through automated issue classification.
Secondary value: product improvement from recurring complaint patterns.
Main gap: unclear consent for uses beyond service delivery.
Next action: validate permissions before testing external scenarios.

output_examples.input: Diagnose the value of weekly logistics data.
output_examples.output: The weakest factor is buyer action because interest lacks paid validation. Run two buyer interviews and a limited pilot before forecasting revenue.

output_examples.input: Prioritize three uses for equipment sensor data.
output: First: predictive maintenance, supported by downtime records and an internal owner.
Second: warranty risk analysis, pending quality checks.
Third: external benchmarking, pending authorization and buyer validation.

best_practices: Provide evidence for each score and label every assumption.
Separate realized benefits, validated opportunities, and speculative potential.
Complete rights and compliance checks before recommending external use.
anti_patterns: Do not treat stated buyer interest as proven willingness to pay.
Do not present potential value as current revenue or asset value.
Do not rank scenarios without considering permissions, quality, and alternatives.

faq.question: Does this skill produce a formal asset valuation?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes value sources and opportunities but does not replace a licensed valuation report.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide data sources, fields, quality, permissions, current uses, candidate buyers, operating costs, and available performance evidence.

faq.question: How are value opportunities classified?
faq.answer: The framework reviews nine types, including revenue, savings, efficiency, risk, decisions, financing, ecosystem, compliance, and strategic options.

faq.question: Can it estimate monetary value?
faq.answer: It can create evidence-based ranges when sufficient inputs exist. Every estimate should state its method, assumptions, and uncertainty.

faq.question: How does it find cross-industry opportunities?
faq.answer: It examines other industries, buyer problems, comparable uses, and complementary datasets. These opportunities still require market and compliance validation.

faq.question: Can it handle confidential data?
faq.answer: Use summaries or approved samples. Follow organizational controls and avoid sharing personal, restricted, or proprietary records without authorization.
